speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) what are the specific steps that the Government is taking to recruit 3,000 preschool teachers by 2020; and (b) considering that less than 1% of preschool educators are men, whether there are plans put in place to recruit more men into this sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To support the expansion of the preschool sector, we have put in place measures to attract more people, both men and women, to join the sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: At present, there are around 18,000 preschool educators in the sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will closely monitor our efforts to grow the sector as we aim to meet our targets.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) also offers training awards to encourage students to pursue Early Childhood courses at the NIEC and the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS).

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These awards provide students with full sponsorship of their course fees, learning resource grants, professional development grant, monthly study allowances and professional networking opportunities, and that are pre-employment efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To attract more mid-career entrants, we have rolled out the Professional Conversion Programme (PCP) for Preschool Teachers and the Place-and-Train Programme (PnT) for Educarers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: People who are looking to switch careers or re-enter the workforce can apply for these programmes, and can earn a salary while undergoing a mix of on-the-job coaching and classroom-based teaching or training.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To facilitate their entry to the sector, the Government provides subsidies for the training courses and salaries.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To provide greater clarity on the career pathways and opportunities for Early Childhood professionals, ECDA, with industry partners, had introduced the Skills Framework for the Early Childhood Sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is supported by moves to retain and support in-service professionals to deepen their skill competencies, such as Professional Development Programmes (PDPs) and the ECDA Fellows Programme.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Apart from manpower programmes, we have been working with industry partners to streamline work processes and reduce educators' administrative workload under the Industry Transformation Map (ITM).

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: More recently, ECDA rolled out a National Campaign for the Early Childhood Sector to create greater awareness of the sector and career opportunities, and to foster greater respect and recognition of the profession.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Through these efforts, we have seen more people, including men, who are interested to join the sector today.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Over the last five years, the intake of mid-career entrants enrolled in professional early childhood certificate or diploma courses have increased by more than 70%.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The intake sizes of Pre-employment Training students for similar courses have also increased by two times, with the proportion of men enrolled in the diploma courses doubling.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In tandem with the expansion of the sector, salaries for early childhood professionals have been rising steadily.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: ECDA expects salary growth for early childhood educators to continue to outpace that of the general market.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: ECDA will continue to work with NIEC and other partners to create more progression opportunities and areas of specialisation, such as in Mother Tongue Language teaching, Learning Support and Early Intervention, and Outdoor Learning.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Some of these areas, such as Outdoor Learning, may provide scope to attract more men to the sector, which at this point in time is a very low proportion.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Together with its partners, ECDA will press on to uplift the early childhood profession and ensure that the preschool sector provides rewarding and meaningful careers.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Could the Minister please share, what are the challenges that the Ministry have faced in trying to increase recruitment in this area as a whole?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are whole range of factors which we have assessed that may make it competitive to bring in more people into the early childhood sector.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: One of them, of course, is more qualitative – it is people's perception of what an early childhood sector job entails.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And there are certain common misconceptions that an early childhood educator is a nanny or a caregiver, rather than a teacher, a person who guides and grows a child in the early years of their development.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, to address that, we have launched, last year, a national campaign.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Having consulted many members of the profession about what kinds of misperceptions people may have and testing with them to see whether it resonates with them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some of the messages, videos and profiles that have gone out seek to address people's minds, for both those who are considering entering the sector, and of course, the parents who influence and guide their children on what kinds of jobs to aspire towards, to have a more accurate view on the importance of early childhood.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Science and data have shown that good early childhood education impacts not just the cognitive development of the child, but the holistic development of children – ages zero to three, zero to six, these are very important ages, and we want to grow the sector.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We attract most of our entrants through career conversion.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Many people, after working in various sectors, decide that they want to enter the sector.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And we find that that is also a very stable group of people.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And the PCP and Place and Train have been very helpful in that regard.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, mindset is one, creating pathways is another to attract people into the sector.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Member also asked about men, whether we are able to attract more men so that we grow the pool of potential applicants into the sector.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And I have spoken to senior educators because I wanted to understand this phenomenon when I joined the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: You know there are very, very few men who are preschool teachers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, I just met one last night at some event.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: One preschool teacher who was a man and the rest were women.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: When I speak to preschool senior educators, they talk about cultural factors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They say that firstly, there is a mindset amongst people that the preschool sector is more suited to women.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Women are very good carers and educators, but I think men can also equally play a role in that regard.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, we continue in this regard, and we hope to achieve our targets as stated.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And just to state that there is no bearing on the generosity of the Budget later either.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 3.30 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 2.54 pm until 3.30 pm.
